subject: pe
title: Foundations: Eleven Components
welcome_lead: Meet the eleven components that build a complete athlete.
meta_desc: GCSE PE Components of Fitness foundations: 5 health-related and 6 skill-related.
final_note: Awesome! You can now name and define all eleven components.

concepts.def: Heart and lungs supplying oxygen for long activity.
Maximal force a muscle can apply.
Range of motion around a joint.
Ratio of fat to lean body mass.

walkthroughs.body_html: The 5 health-related components keep you well: cardiovascular endurance, muscular endurance, strength, flexibility and body composition. Everyone needs them — not just athletes.

The 6 skill-related components win sport: agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time and speed. Power is the only one many syllabi include in both lists, but for GCSE it is treated as skill-related.
Add them up: 5 + 6 = 11 components of fitness. Different sports demand different combinations. A sprinter relies on power, speed and reaction time; a yoga teacher leans on flexibility and balance.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between strength and power?
options: They are the same thing.
Strength is for the upper body, power for the lower.
Strength is maximum force; power is force times speed of movement.
Doing less over time.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between aerobic and muscular endurance?
options: Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
Aerobic endurance is the cardiovascular system's ability to supply oxygen; muscular endurance is a muscle's ability to contract repeatedly without fatigue.
They are different names for the same component.
Doing less over time.
Doing less over time.
Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
Gradually increasing training demands so the body keeps adapting.
Training as hard as possible immediately.
